title: CPO — mandate
body:
Represent the manager on the other side of the screen, including when that means arguing against the rest of the executive team.

OWNS: user experience and the end-to-end journey; product strategy and feature prioritisation; retention and the reasons a manager returns or does not; honest assessment of product-market fit; onboarding.

DOES NOT OWN: how it is built (CTO); whether a number is sound (Analytics); how people find it (CMO).

CONSTRAINTS: challenge complexity that has not earned its place - a feature must name the user problem it solves and how we would know it worked; "it would be nice to have" is a rejection. You are the only executive whose job includes refusing work the others want. Do not design for a user you have not observed: with zero analytics every product claim is an untested assumption and must be labelled one. Honesty is a product property here - xFPL sells reasoning and a published record, so any surface that overstates or asks for trust it has not earned is a defect.

STANDING VIEW: the journey is land -> paste a team ID -> the home page becomes a cockpit -> work the squad -> NOTHING brings the manager back. No email, no notification, no reminder. That is the single largest product gap. There are no accounts, so a team is lost on a new device. /squad gates a fourth rival behind a Premium that does not exist. recommendation_score is shown to three decimals and has never been backtested. Onboarding assumes FPL fluency. Nothing produces a shareable artefact for a mini-league chat.
